t: Nothing in this Act may be construed to affect or modify any treaty or other right of the Ute Indian Tribe or any other Indian tribe.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the mention of an Indian tribe, which is an outside party, signals participation. But this is only a savings clause that preserves existing treaty and other rights. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue over a federal decision, so no outside party is brought into any federal decision-making process.
fable.s: Nothing in this Act may be construed to affect or modify any treaty or other right of the Ute Indian Tribe or any other Indian tribe.

qwen_block.w: This section is a savings clause that preserves existing treaty rights. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, public comment, or advisory input from outside parties regarding federal decisions. It merely states that the Act does not alter pre-existing legal rights.
qwen_block.s: Nothing in this Act may be construed to affect or modify any treaty or other right of the Ute Indian Tribe or any other Indian tribe.

opus.w: This is a savings clause that keeps existing tribal treaty and other rights in place. It does not require or allow the federal government to consult or coordinate with tribes, or anyone else outside the government, before a decision. The tribe is mentioned, but it plays no part in any federal decision, so this is not participation.
opus.s: Nothing in this Act may be construed to affect or modify any treaty or other right of the Ute Indian Tribe or any other Indian tribe.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The section names the Ute Indian Tribe and other tribes, which are outside the federal government. That could look like tribal consultation. But the section is only a savings clause. It keeps existing treaty rights in place and sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue over a federal decision. Having a tribe named is not enough under the definition.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a savings clause that preserves existing treaty rights but does not require any active participation, consultation, or coordination with the Ute Indian Tribe or any other tribe. It does not establish a process for outside parties to influence federal decisions, nor does it grant rights to sue or participate in advisory bodies. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: Nothing in this Act may be construed to affect or modify any treaty or other right of the Ute Indian Tribe or any other Indian tribe.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that mentioning the Ute Indian Tribe implies some form of consultation or recognition of their rights that constitutes participation. However, the text is a "savings clause" that merely preserves existing legal rights; it does not mandate any specific process, consultation, hearing, or interaction between the federal government and the tribe for the purposes of this Act. It does not require the government to consult with the tribe before making a decision, nor does it grant them a right to sue or participate in an advisory capacity. It simply states that the Act does not override existing treaties.
